## Fish Scale Analysis

order of operations

- Add/stage

- commit button (RStudio)

  - write commit message

  - commit button (window)

  - pull

  - push

Load the tidyverse and the dataset

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
fish_data <- read_csv("../data/Gaeta_etal_CLC_data.csv")
```

Observe the dataset

```{r}
head(fish_data)
```

Summary statistics for fish scale length

```{r}
fish_data |> 
  summarize(min_scale_length = min(scalelength, na.rm = T), 
            max_scale_length = max(scalelength, na.rm = T), 
            mean_scale_length = mean(scalelength, na.rm = T))
```

You discover that the device used to measure the scale length of the fish in `Gaeta_etal_CLC_data.csv` is not accurate for those smaller than 1 mm.

In the `fish_analysis.qmd` file, create a new data frame that does not include fish with scale lengths of less than 1 mm from `fish_data`. The new dataset will have 4,029 rows (see answer key).

Use the `write_csv()` function to save this new data frame as a CSV file. It should be in an appropriate sub-directory.

Commit this change to version control with a good commit message.

Once you've made the commit, push the commit to your repo. Pop over to GitHub to ensure that the `.qmd` file and the new dataset are there.

